observations.statement: Six catalog entries bind Docker Manager UI locations to commands and handlers: host refresh, host session launch, hosts open, image, image delete, and image inspect.
Host refresh, host session launch, and hosts open are event effects with one declared event reference apiece and event tests requiring command_id, origin, correlation_id, and handler target.

Image, image delete, and image inspect declare no expected event types and instead require receipt effects plus tests that allow an explicit no-persist route/open disposition and prohibit unexpected persisted domain events.
Every entry names an availability selector and disabled-reason projection used before dispatch.
Every entry specifies a stable role/name/description, keyboard activation, deterministic focus restoration after dispatch or error, and assistive-technology exposure of its disabled reason.
Production certification for every entry requires render/control, dispatcher, typed payload/result, state projection, disabled-reason, receipt/event, accessibility, and regression evidence.

candidate_findings.title: Concrete command payload and result contracts are absent
candidate_findings.statement: The six entries require typed args or payload and result contracts but do not define argument or result type names, required fields, validation rules, success variants, or error variants within the assigned core.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders and test authors cannot derive a single interoperable dispatcher boundary or an exact typed acceptance oracle from these entries.

candidate_findings.title: Receipt-only commands do not define successful operational outcomes
candidate_findings.statement: For cmd.docker.image, cmd.docker.image.delete, and cmd.docker.image.inspect, the only declared effect is a receipt while the required test also permits an explicit no-persist route/open disposition; the core does not specify the resulting route, displayed inspection data, deletion completion or state change, or success and failure receipt fields.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders retain consequential discretion over user-visible and domain outcomes, and the listed evidence can pass without proving that the named operation completed.

candidate_findings.title: Failure and effect-emission semantics are unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The contracts require preserving a result and receipt or event effect and restoring focus after an error, but do not state which validation or handler failures produce an event or receipt, the error result shape, whether partial effects are possible, or what user-visible failure state is projected.
candidate_findings.impact: Failures can yield divergent event history, receipts, focus behavior, and retry affordances while still satisfying the named evidence categories.

candidate_findings.title: Availability state lifecycle and authority are undefined
candidate_findings.statement: All six controls name selector paths and disabled-reason paths, but the core provides no value schema, derivation rules, update authority, transition timing, or consistency rule between availability and disabled copy.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can enable controls at different times, publish stale reasons, or disagree during in-flight and failed dispatches.

candidate_findings.title: Duplicate, concurrent, retry, and cancellation behavior is unconstrained
candidate_findings.statement: The dispatch and effect obligations do not define serialization, deduplication or idempotency, in-flight re-dispatch, retry, timeout, or cancellation behavior for any of the six commands.
candidate_findings.impact: Repeated activation can create nondeterministic handler calls, receipts or events, and UI state while an operation is already in flight.

candidate_findings.title: Accessibility assertions lack exact semantic and focus oracles
candidate_findings.statement: The accessibility contracts require a stable role/name/description matching each command and deterministic focus return, but do not name the exact role, accessible name or description, focus destination, or behavior if the originating control becomes unavailable.
candidate_findings.impact: Incompatible accessible presentations can all appear compliant, and regression tests lack exact expected values.

candidate_findings.title: Correlation evidence persistence and consumers are unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: Event effects must record dispatch correlation evidence and receipt commands name receipt references, but the core does not state the evidence schema, storage or retention behavior, write authority, lookup interface, or consuming surface.
candidate_findings.impact: Certification can prove that an effect was asserted without ensuring traceability is durable, authoritative, or consumable.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: The UI location, command identifier, and handler target are explicit for all six entries.
The core explicitly distinguishes event effects for the three host-oriented commands from receipt effects for the three image-oriented commands.
The receipt-only command tests explicitly prohibit unexpected persisted domain events.
Role/name/description, keyboard access, focus handling, and disabled-state announcement are each explicit accessibility dimensions for every control.
The categories of evidence required before production certification are explicit for every entry.

unknowns.statement: The assigned core does not identify the downstream consumers of emitted events or dispatch receipts after handler dispatch.
Whether each declared event is emitted on handler entry, request acceptance, successful completion, or failure is not stated.
Whether the receipt-only commands mutate non-persisted or external state despite emitting no persisted domain event is not determined.
Whether availability and disabled-reason projections are snapshots or reactive values, and how they change while dispatch is in flight, is not stated.
